# What the market evidence can and cannot yet say (RQ3 and H6) {#sec-markets}

The title of this section was fixed before any post-seal return was read, by the pre-registered plausibility rule D11 (@sec-methods; @sec-app-pap). The rule compares the minimum detectable effect (MDE) of the primary H5 test with a threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD of exposure. The primary MDE, at {{< var power.power_pct >}}% power and at Holm's first-step level of {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}, is {{< var d11.primary_mde >}} pp per SD. It exceeds the threshold, so the rule fires: RQ3 is reported under this title, and the paper is led by RQ1 and RQ2 (@sec-rq1, @sec-rq2). The threshold was written into the plan before the power analysis first ran, but became binding only when it was confirmed with the MDE in view, and should be weighed as such (PAP §7). The MDE is printed beside every market null below.

## The confirmatory test of H5 and H5b

@tbl-rq3-confirmatory reproduces the record of the single confirmatory run (@sec-methods), which used all {{< var rq3.provenance.n >}} FF49 industries (dropped for a missing return: {{< var rq3.provenance.dropped >}}) and {{< var rq3.provenance.n_days >}} factor days from {{< var design.window.start >}} to {{< var design.window.end >}}. The primary null is D21's b = b̄, the mean slope of the same exposure vector over {{< var power.n_windows >}} overlapping pre-seal windows ({{< var design.null_years >}}); the statistic is (b̂ − b̄)/s, referred to a t distribution with {{< var power.t_df >}} degrees of freedom. For H5, b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5.b_pp2 >}} pp per SD against b̄ = {{< var rq3.h5.bbar >}} and s = {{< var rq3.h5.s >}}, so T = {{< var rq3.h5.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5.p >}}. For H5b, which holds the AIOE benchmark [@felten2021occupational] in the regression, b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5b.b_pp2 >}} against b̄ = {{< var rq3.h5b.bbar >}} and s = {{< var rq3.h5b.s >}}, so T = {{< var rq3.h5b.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5b.p >}}. Neither p reaches the first-step level, so Holm's procedure [@holm1979simple] stops there: H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}}, and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}.

{{< include _generated/tables/rq3-confirmatory.md >}}

Every number in @tbl-rq3-confirmatory carries the S1 timing caveat (PAP §10). Design B is out of sample in its AEI data only; it is not strictly real-time. Its OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} weights were released on {{< var design.s1.oews_release >}}, after the formation date of {{< var design.formation >}} and inside the return window, and its O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} task links also postdate formation, although their task text is byte-identical to that of O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.r32 >}} (PAP §11). R32, the strict real-time row, rebuilds the exposure on the OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}} weights that were public at formation. It gives b̂ = {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} for H5 (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r32.h5.p >}}) and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b ([{{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r32.h5b.p >}}). R1, built on the later OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r1 >}} weights, is look-ahead; it gives {{< var rob.r01.h5.estimate >}} for H5 and {{< var rob.r01.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b (@sec-robustness).

The co-primary specifications share the run and the table. R12 replaces exposure by its standardised ranks. R13 drops Softw, the industry with the largest Design B `z_delegation` ({{< var audit.exposure.b.z_del_max >}} SD). Under R12 both slopes are negative: {{< var rq3.h5_r12.b >}} for H5 (T = {{< var rq3.h5_r12.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5_r12.p_primary >}}) and {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.b >}} for H5b (T = {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.p_primary >}}). Under R13 they are {{< var rq3.h5_r13.b >}} (T = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.p_primary >}}) and {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.b >}} (T = {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.p_primary >}}), each on its own, larger scale (s = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.s >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.s >}}). The claim that delegation exposure is priced in this window beyond the historical pattern required a primary rejection together with an R13 rejection at the same Holm level. No primary is rejected, so the co-condition is not met for either hypothesis.

## The fixed wording

PAP §3.3 (P14) fixes the wording of a non-rejection, and the confirmatory script printed it for each hypothesis. Verbatim from the record behind @tbl-rq3-confirmatory, with the S1 caveat above (R32):

> {{< var rq3.h5.wording >}}

> {{< var rq3.h5b.wording >}}

The paper does not paraphrase these sentences into a statement that the market did not price delegation. Their null is narrower than the approved hypothesis (@sec-methods): a rejection would have said that the slope departs from what this exposure vector showed over {{< var design.null_years >}}, not that it differs from zero. Because b̄ is not zero, this null makes a positive finding harder and a negative one easier to reach than the zero null would, a property of the test's geometry (PAP §3.3, D21).

## Intervals, the R13 MDE and the secondary null

Two intervals are reported for each hypothesis, b̂ ± c·s at each Holm level. For H5 they are [{{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}] pp per SD at {{< var design.alpha.h5_second >}} and [{{< var rq3.h5.ci_0025.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5.ci_0025.hi_pp2 >}}] at {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}. For H5b they are [{{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}] and [{{< var rq3.h5b.ci_0025.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5b.ci_0025.hi_pp2 >}}]. The primary MDEs are {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} pp for H5 and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp for H5b. The co-conditioned claim has R13's larger MDE at the first-step level, {{< var rq3.h5.mde_r13 >}} pp for H5 and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde_r13 >}} pp for H5b, so a pricing claim robust to dropping Softw had {{< var power.power_pct >}}% power only near those values (@tbl-rq3-confirmatory).

The zero-slope statistic from the same run is a secondary null and is not part of the decision. For H5 the secondary null of a zero slope gives T = {{< var rq3.h5.b0.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5.b0.p >}}, beside an MDE of {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} pp per SD (the same s and first-step critical as the primary). For H5b it gives T = {{< var rq3.h5b.b0.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5b.b0.p >}}, beside an MDE of {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp. Both carry the S1 caveat (R32). They answer the approved H5 wording literally, whether more exposed industries earned different risk-adjusted returns, which D21 narrowed to a departure from the historical pattern (@sec-methods).

The robustness rows that move b̂ most are reported in full in @sec-robustness and @sec-app-robustness-tables. Each carries the S1 caveat and none changes a decision (PAP §8.1); intervals are at the {{< var design.alpha.h5_second >}} level. For H5, R7, which drops Hardw, Softw and Chips, gives {{< var rob.r07.h5.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5.p >}}); R12, the ranks, gives {{< var rq3.h5_r12.b >}}; and R5, equal-weighted industry returns, gives {{< var rob.r05.h5.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r05.h5.p >}}). For H5b, R12 gives {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.b >}}; R7 gives {{< var rob.r07.h5b.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5b.p >}}); and R6 on the FF30 industries gives {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.p >}}).

## Secondary inference

The design specification named randomisation inference as the test. On pre-seal windows it rejected far more often than its nominal level, since industries with similar exposure co-move, so it is kept as secondary, each p printed with its documented size at a nominal {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}} (@sec-methods). With {{< var rq3.secondary.n_permutations >}} permutations each, permuting `z_delegation` gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.ri_h5 >}} for H5 (documented size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.ri_h5 >}}%). Permuting `z_delegation` with `z_aioe` held in place gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.ri_h5b >}} for H5b (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.ri_h5b >}}%, oversized even under exchangeability). The Freedman–Lane scheme [@freedman1983nonstochastic; @winkler2014permutation] gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.fl_h5b >}} for H5b when scored by the pivotal t (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.fl_pivotal_h5b >}}%) and {{< var rq3.secondary.fl_coef_h5b >}} when scored by the coefficient (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.fl_coef_h5b >}}%). Each p is read against its size. Conventional OLS with HC3 standard errors, for reference, gives {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5_b >}} (SE {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5_se >}}) for H5 and {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5b_b >}} (SE {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5b_se >}}) for H5b. None of these enters the decision.

## The influence of Softw

@tbl-rq3-influence-softw reports Softw's influence on the confirmatory fits, post-result diagnostics that PAP §3.3 (P11) places outside the decision. Softw's leverage is {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.leverage >}} in the H5 fit and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.leverage >}} in the H5b fit. Its DFBETAS on b are {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.dfbetas >}} and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.dfbetas >}}, and its Cook's distances are {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.cooks_d >}} and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.cooks_d >}}. The industries with the largest Cook's distance in each fit, listed in @tbl-rq3-influence-top, are Gold and Hardw, not Softw. This agrees with the R13 estimates lying close to the primaries.

## Exploratory market analyses

Exploratory: Design A forms exposure from AEI releases and reads returns from the market seal, {{< var design.seal_date >}}, to {{< var design.window.end >}} (PAP §8.3, D19). `A_r2` uses release r2 alone and is numerically identical to Design B, so the Design B rows below are the `A_r2` rows over a sub-window and are not independent evidence. `A_pooled`, which is look-ahead, pools releases r2 to r6, and r3 to r6 were published during and after the return window (PAP §10). Its largest `z_delegation`, again {{< var audit.exposure.a_pooled.z_del_max_industry >}}, is {{< var audit.exposure.a_pooled.z_del_max >}} SD. Design A is exploratory because general knowledge of post-seal market moves cannot be removed (PAP §0.4); nothing here tests H5 or H5b or carries error control.

Exploratory: the event studies use the D19 rule. The events are ChatGPT, which the design specification names, and every flagship model announcement by OpenAI, Anthropic or Google's AI labs in a named source over the period the rule fixes (@tbl-rq3-event-dates). Day zero is the first trading day on or after the announcement, and @tbl-rq3-event-days lists moved dates and overlapping windows. The rule's exceptions (excluding Gemma and Gemini Ultra, adding ChatGPT by name, accepting an OpenAI release's absence from the source) were chosen with the source's list, and so the dates, in view (PAP §0.4). Each industry's cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over an FF5+UMD fit [@fama2015five; @carhart1997persistence] is regressed across industries on exposure, with HC3 standard errors.

Exploratory: @tbl-rq3-event-slopes and @fig-rq3-event-slopes report every event, horizon and design. For ChatGPT, the `A_r2` slope is {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.b >}} pp of CAR per SD at the shorter horizon (CI [{{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.p >}}) and {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.b >}} at the longer one ([{{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.p >}}). The p-values are nominal and single-test, and may be oversized because abnormal returns are correlated across industries on a common date.

{{< include _generated/tables/rq3-event-slopes.md >}}

{{< include _generated/figures/rq3-event-slopes.md >}}

Exploratory: the tercile portfolios go long the highest-exposure third of FF49 industries and short the lowest, with membership fixed at formation, monthly capitalisation weights and equal-weighted legs beside them (PAP §8.3, D19). They report CAPM, FF3 and FF5+UMD alphas [@fama1993common] with Newey–West errors [@newey1987simple; @newey1994automatic], stationary-bootstrap intervals [@politis1994stationary], the probabilistic Sharpe ratio, PSR [@bailey2012sharpe], and the deflated Sharpe ratio, DSR [@bailey2014deflated]. They are measurement devices that express the cross-sectional slope as a return spread, not strategies; the costed versions show the spread's fragility, not a tradable return (@tbl-rq3-terciles-b-cap-costs).

Exploratory: for Design B (secondary) with cap-weighted legs, the annualised mean high-minus-low return is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.estimate >}} pp (bootstrap CI [{{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.p >}}). The FF3 alpha is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff3.estimate >}} pp and the FF5+UMD alpha {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.estimate >}} pp ([{{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.p >}}). That spread across factor models rests on {{< var design.window.months >}} monthly returns and is model-fragile (@tbl-rq3-terciles-b-cap). The PSR is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.psr.estimate >}} and the DSR {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.dsr.estimate >}}; with equal-weighted legs they are {{< var rq3.terciles.b.ew.psr.estimate >}} and {{< var rq3.terciles.b.ew.dsr.estimate >}}. For `A_r2` with cap-weighted legs they are {{< var rq3.terciles.a_r2.cap.psr.estimate >}} and {{< var rq3.terciles.a_r2.cap.dsr.estimate >}}; for `A_pooled`, look-ahead, {{< var rq3.terciles.a_pooled.cap.psr.estimate >}} and {{< var rq3.terciles.a_pooled.cap.dsr.estimate >}} (@tbl-rq3-terciles-dsr). The DSR treats every variant as an independent trial, which overstates the number of independent trials: B is nested in `A_r2`, and `A_r2` and `A_pooled` hold nearly the same portfolios (@fig-rq3-tercile-cumulative).

Exploratory: the comparison with Eisfeldt, Schubert and Zhang [@eisfeldt2023generative], who report higher returns for more exposed firms, asks only for the sign of the CAR slope on `z_aioe` around the ChatGPT release, before `z_delegation` is added. At the FF49 level, which is not their firm-level design, the slope in the first step is {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.b >}} pp of CAR per SD of `z_aioe` (CI [{{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.p >}}; @tbl-rq3-eisfeldt-step1). The sign is negative and the interval contains zero, so their sign is not reproduced at this level of aggregation. @tbl-rq3-eisfeldt-step2 adds `z_delegation` for `A_r2` and for `A_pooled` (look-ahead).

## Talk versus use (H6, exploratory)

Exploratory: H6 (PAP §6, D18) belongs to no testing family. The talk index T of an FF49 industry is the share of its filers whose annual reports match at least one primary AI term in the SEC EDGAR full-text search [@sec2026edgar]. The gap uses filings dated {{< var h6.talk.filed_start >}} to {{< var h6.talk.filed_end >}}, public before formation. Pooled across all filers, the share rises from {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2019 >}} in the first filing year of the series to {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2024 >}} in {{< var h6.talk.year >}} and {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2025 >}} in the last (@tbl-h6-talk-by-year, @fig-h6-talk-by-year). Over the same years the share of filers with no FF49 industry rises from {{< var h6.talk.unmapped_share_pct.y2019 >}}% to {{< var h6.talk.unmapped_share_pct.y2025 >}}%, so part of that trend is composition; the mapped-only series runs from {{< var h6.talk.pooled_mapped.y2019 >}} to {{< var h6.talk.pooled_mapped.y2025 >}}.

{{< include _generated/tables/h6-talk-by-year.md >}}

{{< include _generated/figures/h6-talk-by-year.md >}}

Exploratory: across industries, the Spearman correlation of T with Design B `z_usage` (conversations matched to O\*NET tasks, weighted to industries) is {{< var h6.spearman.rho >}}, with an industry-bootstrap CI of [{{< var h6.spearman.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.spearman.ci.hi >}}] (@tbl-h6-divergence, @fig-h6-talk-vs-usage). Its p, from the t-approximation with n minus two degrees of freedom, is {{< var diag.h6.none.p >}}. That p is nominal and exploratory, a post-result addition logged among the deviations of PAP §11 (@sec-app-deviations), in no testing family. Two inputs are fixed at retrieval, not in {{< var h6.talk.year >}}. The FF49 industry is each filer's current SIC from the EDGAR submissions file, retrieved at {{< var h6.vintage.submissions_retrieved_utc >}} and applied to every filing year (PAP §11). The numerator uses the full-text search's phrase matching as the SEC implemented it on the retrieval date (PAP §6).

Exploratory: the leave-one-industry-out Spearman in @tbl-diag-h6-influence is a post-result diagnostic (PAP §11, deviations); exploratory; not a decision. Leaving out Softw gives {{< var diag.h6.softw.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.softw.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.softw.ci_hi >}}]). Leaving out Hardw gives {{< var diag.h6.hardw.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.hardw.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.hardw.ci_hi >}}]) and leaving out BusSv {{< var diag.h6.bussv.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.bussv.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.bussv.ci_hi >}}]); both intervals cross zero, and every leave-out is in the table. Three parts of R29 also have intervals that cover zero: the change in talk from the first filing year to {{< var h6.talk.year >}} gives {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_hi >}}]), filers weighted by public float give {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_hi >}}]), and filings dated before formation in the formation year give {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.estimate >}} ([{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_hi >}}]; @sec-robustness).

Exploratory: the gap is the standardised residual of z(T) on `z_usage` (@tbl-h6-gap-ranking). Its return association is the confirmatory regression with the gap in place of `z_delegation`, with s, b̄ and q recomputed for the gap vector on the same pre-seal windows (@tbl-h6-gap-returns). It gives b̂ = {{< var h6.gap_returns.b >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD of gap, with interval [{{< var h6.gap_returns.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.gap_returns.ci.hi >}}], and T = {{< var h6.gap_returns.t_bbar >}} with nominal p = {{< var h6.gap_returns.p_bbar >}} against b = b̄; against the secondary null of a zero slope, T = {{< var h6.gap_returns.t_zero >}} and nominal p = {{< var h6.gap_returns.p_zero >}}; no MDE computed (exploratory). It is in no testing family and carries Design B's S1 caveat.

## What a future window would need

The MDE is a fixed multiple of the null scale: MDE = {{< var power.mde_over_s >}} × s, where s is the observed spread of the historical slope across windows of {{< var design.window.months >}} months (@sec-methods). With s = {{< var power.s.h5 >}} for H5 and {{< var power.s.h5b >}} for H5b, the MDEs are {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp per SD. In units of that spread, a window of this length detects reliably only a departure of {{< var power.mde_over_s >}} historical standard deviations from the {{< var design.null_years >}} pattern. For the H5 MDE to fall to the plausibility threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp, a future window's s would have to be no larger than that threshold divided by {{< var power.mde_over_s >}}. A claim that also survives dropping Softw would need the same of R13's scale, whose MDEs are {{< var rq3.h5.mde_r13 >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde_r13 >}} pp.

No generated file computes s for a longer window or a later formation release, so how far either would move it is unknown here. What the market evidence can say is bounded by {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp per SD: the confirmatory test was run as registered, H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}} and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}, in the P14 wording above. What it cannot yet say is whether this exposure vector is priced by a departure smaller than those values (@tbl-rq3-confirmatory).
